name: flume
baseline: std::sync::mpsc (the claim was charted against the pre-1.67 implementation)
verdict_reason: The README's 'always faster than std::sync::mpsc' was charted against the old std channel. Since Rust 1.67 std::sync::mpsc is crossbeam-channel's algorithm, which the same README says flume beats only 'sometimes', so the 'always' no longer holds as stated. No text numbers exist either way.
tier_reason: The only numbers are in a chart image from crossbeam's benchmark suite, run by the author on a stated machine.
claimed_speedup: README: 'Always faster than `std::sync::mpsc` and sometimes `crossbeam-channel`'; the only numbers are in a chart from crossbeam's benchmark suite (AMD Ryzen 7 3700x, Linux kernel 5.11.2).
workload: crossbeam-channel benchmark suite (seq, spsc, mpsc, mpmc over bounded and unbounded channels).
one_liner: MPMC channel with sync and async APIs and no unsafe code; its 'always faster than std mpsc' chart predates std adopting crossbeam's design.
how_it_is_fast: A single mutex-protected queue with a carefully kept short critical section, plus a signal depot for waking blocked senders and receivers. Avoiding unsafe code keeps the design simple; speed comes from minimal work under the lock rather than lock-free structures.
use_it_when: You want one channel type usable from both sync and async code
MPMC or select-style waiting with timeouts on stable Rust
skip_it_when: Single-consumer sync channels on Rust 1.67+, where std::sync::mpsc needs no dependency and no current numbers show flume ahead
caveats: Chart image only; no numbers in text.
The chart predates Rust 1.67 (Linux 5.11.2 era), so its std mpsc is the old implementation.
A 2025 chart in kanal's README (rustc 1.85.1) includes both flume and std::sync::mpsc and does not show flume ahead of std in the bounded SPSC tests (chart reading, not a quotable number).
The README carries a 'casual maintenance' badge.
tradeoffs: Lock-based queue: under heavy contention throughput depends on the mutex.
Optional spin feature trades CPU for latency on some platforms.

evidence.quote: Tests were performed on an AMD Ryzen 7 3700x with 8/16 cores running Linux kernel 5.11.2 with the bfq scheduler.
No `unsafe` code anywhere in the codebase!
in this release the implementation is switched out to be based on crossbeam-channel
